sentences.text: After final command approval, orbit state management remains under continuous control so that operations users work from a common predicted trajectory.
The Orbit Determination Engine fits dynamic orbit solutions using radiometric tracking, spacecraft telemetry timing, force models, and the latest approved maneuver history.
Tracking arcs include measurements associated with the North S-Band Antenna, South S-Band Antenna, Kiruna X-Band Antenna, and Svalbard X-Band Antenna when those data meet quality and timing criteria.
The Product Quality Service checks each orbit solution for frame consistency, covariance reasonableness, time-tag continuity, and agreement with recent contact predictions.
The Flight Dynamics Team uses the residual report to separate station-related tracking biases from dynamic model errors before accepting an orbit solution.
The Flight Dynamics Facility maintains the authoritative orbit catalog for the ground segment and records the modeling assumptions applied to each accepted solution.
Maneuver screening evaluates orbit maintenance options against fuel use, ground contact visibility, payload outage constraints, and post-burn tracking opportunities.
For each candidate burn, the Flight Dynamics Team computes expected state change, execution tolerance, recovery strategy, and the earliest time when the solution can be declared stable.
Collision assessment uses externally supplied conjunction data together with the current covariance to estimate miss distance, encounter geometry, and probability of collision.
The Flight Dynamics Team maintains screening rules that distinguish routine catalog monitoring from events requiring immediate operator notification.
If the predicted risk exceeds the mission threshold, the Spacecraft Operations Team receives a maneuver recommendation package that includes timing constraints and operational impacts.
Attitude geometry support translates the predicted orbit into Sun angle, Earth limb, lunar exclusion, target visibility, and antenna pointing information for daily operations.
The Flight Dynamics Facility sends the Star Tracker Mask File after verifying predicted bright-object exclusions against the current attitude plan.
Bluebell requires that each flight dynamics delivery include a validity interval, coordinate frame, generation time, and operational use statement.

The Flight Dynamics Facility distributes routine ephemerides and event predictions through controlled interfaces used by the Mission Control Center, Mission Planning System, and Payload Processing Facility.
The Mission Planning System uses accepted orbit files to align imaging requests, contact opportunities, recorder margins, and downlink windows.
The Command Validation Gateway checks maneuver command parameters against the screened burn plan before allowing the command stack to proceed.
The Flight Dynamics Team produces the Ephemeris Delta Note when updated state vectors change predicted acquisition times or imaging geometry beyond agreed thresholds.
The Orbit Determination Engine produces the Laser Retroreflector Window from the refined orbit solution and the approved station geometry constraints.
The Spacecraft Operations Team receives maneuver recommendations with enough lead time to rehearse commanding, verify contingency actions, and coordinate contact coverage.
The Payload Calibration Team obtains predicted viewing geometry from flight dynamics products to interpret instrument trends and plan calibration activities.
The Network Control System uses antenna pointing predictions derived from the accepted ephemeris to prepare scheduled contacts and verify tracking readiness.
The Long Term Archive retains released orbit products, covariance data, maneuver records, and quality decisions so that later processing can reproduce the operational context.
When the Primary Processing Cluster is unavailable, the Backup Processing Cluster supports product generation with the same validation checks and distribution rules.
